steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat egg whites until foamy in a large glass or metal mixing bowl until stiff peaks form. Lift your beater or whisk straight up: the egg whites should form a sharp peak that holds its shape.

Beat the egg yolks, sugar, butter, and milk together in a large bowl. Stir in the pineapple and bread. Lightly fold egg whites into the pineapple mixture, then spread the mixture into a large baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 35 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Scalloped Pineapple Souffle
raw_recipe.description: This bread pudding-style side dish is light and fluffy, and pairs perfectly with your favorite Easter ham.

review.reviewBody: I wanted to add some additional information about my recipe: This easter I had a diabetic aunt come for dinner so I substituted all of the sugar in the recipe with Splenda. It turned out perfectly. I was afraid that it might need the sugar for consistency/thickness but it was great with the Splenda. I'll be making it this way from now on.

I make this for every ham dinner, holiday or not. It is so good and I always get so many compliments. I have made minor changes to make it better. I use 1 cup of sugar instead of 1-1/2. Too sweet with more. I also add a bit more pineapples I bought the 20oz can and it called for the 15 oz so I used all of it. Also used 3 cups bread and only a dash more. All of the above makes it tastier and not so sweet. Thanks Kaylene for a great recipe

I made this using half the amount of sugar (3/4 cup), and still found it a bit sweet. However, my husband really liked it and didn't think it was too sweet at all. I think it would be great as a side dish to ham--where the salty meat would be an excellent contrast to the sweet fruity taste of this dish. Mine also took a lot longer to bake--like 60 minutes. I think adding in some lemon zest/ juice as another reviewer stated would be an excellent idea to brighten it up a bit. Otherwise, it was just ok for me, but really good to hubby! Thanks for sharing your recipe!

I made this for the first time today for Easter dinner. As I got to step three, I was confused about adding the sugar as I had added all the sugar during step 2. My sons girlfriend helped me to figure out that I was probably supposed to add a small amount of sugar. Hence "Gradually add sugar, continuing to beat until stiff peaks form." I decided to persevere. It took a long time whip up to stiff peak stage. It had a texture like a meringue. I used my kitchenaid stand mixer. 

Then I combined the yolks, butter & milk which didn't incorporate smoothly probably for lack of sugar. I added pineapple and bread (used Country White as per another reviewer) and then it went together better. I also added a teaspoon of fresh lemon zest to batter. I folded in the egg white/sugar and popped it in a glass baking dish lined with parchment. It filled up the 11x7 inch pan. I was afraid that it would puff up and overflow. It did puff up a little bit but didn't overflow. Then it kinda flattened out when I took it out of the oven. The end result- it was really delicious. Everybody loved it. There was nothing left. Scalloped Pineapple was a great accompaniment to Ham.
I made this for Easter today, it was delicious. I used 3/4 cup of sugar instead of the 1 1/2 cup in the recipe. I will certainly make it again.

I Love this! My Mom makes this and I have made a few changes. I prefer day old bread, like a sourdough, or country white. Not wonder bread...too gummy. I use the whole rings of pineapple and cut in 1/4's. It adds a different dimention if 1/4 cup or less...to taste, of citrus zest is used. Orange is fantastic, but I like Lime or lemon best. Do not skimp on the Butter! This is sooo yummy!

I received this recipe from a friend and now make it for Christmas and Easter when we have ham. At Thanksgiving I used a can of Ocean Spray whole cranberry sauce instead of pineapple and it was fantastic with Turkey.

I made this for a family gathering birthday/ Easter celebration yesterday! It was a HUGE hit. Gonna do a little tweaking next time. I used Hawaiian sweet bread, so I'm gonna cut back on the sugar by 1/2 a cup. I thought it was a tad sweet. Also, it was a little juicy. I'm not the best cook in the family and I will definitely use a strainer next time to get all the juice out of the pineapple 🤷‍♀️ other than that, it will be even better next time fer sure!

I am a stickler for properly naming food so it is not misleading! For me this leans more to a bread pudding , as somebody else mentioned. Scalloped implies sause or high percentage of dairy. Though milk is called for it is a trivial ampunt compared to bread. It eats more like a bread pudding than say a scalloped potato. Outside of the poor naming convention I found it meh. My Personal choice will be to add something else next time I make it : mint? Basil? Pepperoncini? I would like more of a flavor Pop. It's a good base. I look forward to experimenting!
I made this for Easter. Everyone loved it. The only thing I did different was to spray the glass casserole dish. I was afraid it might stick with all the pineapple and sugar. It worked out well.
Wonderful recipe. I added 1 cup coconut and 1 cup chopped pecans. Got alot of compliments. Very light and not too sweet. Definitely a keeper.
Easy to make. Tastes great. Love it!
A great family recipe. Will make a double batch next time. Family loved it.

This recipe is way too sweet for me, as written. I will admit to not *exactly* following instructions and having to back-track & fix things. So, #1: maybe less sugar next time? #2: Can I use chunk pineapple instead of crushed? Is there a size in between? #3: Use a casserole dish instead of a 13x9 baking pan. I'm gonna try again!
I made this exactly like the recipe and it was amazing! Made it for Easter and it was perfect with the ham. My entire family loved it!

This was just okay. The egg whites took forever to peak and did not really add all that much. I'll stick to a simpler pineapple stuffing recipe that will yield a great product with much less work next time. Also agree with the review that is is not named properly.
Is it ok to substitute butter with oil?
Veganized every thing. Made my own homemade vegan bread. For all the vegans please tell me how it taste.
This is simply a bread pudding, but if you want to call it something fancy, I guess this would fit the bill. I've made this for years and I've never found anyone who didn't like it.
